title: General Motors Co 8-K: Item 5.02 Departure or Appointment of Directors or Officers
text: Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. On October 23, 2026, Christopher T. Hatto, Vice President, Global Business Solutions and Chief Accounting Officer of General Motors Company (the “Company”), notified the Company of his decision to retire, effective April 1, 2027 (the “Retirement Date”). Mr. Hatto’s decision to retire is not the result of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company’s operations, policies or practices. Mr. Hatto will continue to serve as the Company’s principal accounting officer through the Retirement Date to support an orderly transition. The Company will announce the appointment of a successor principal accounting officer at a later date.

title: General Motors Co 8-K: Item 3.01 Notice of Delisting or Transfer of Listing; Item 5.03 Amendments to Articles or Bylaws; Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure; Item 9.01 Financial Statements and Exhibits
text: Item 3.01. Notice of Delisting or Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule or Standard; Transfer of Listing. On October 26, 2026, the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of General Motors Company (the “Company”) authorized the Company to voluntarily withdraw the listing of its common stock, par value $0.01 per share (the “Common Stock”), from the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) and transfer the listing of the Common Stock to the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) has approved such listing. The Company expects the listing and trading of the Common Stock on the NYSE to cease at the close of trading on November 16, 2026. The Company expects the Common Stock to begin trading on Nasdaq on November 17, 2026. Following the transfer to Nasdaq, the Common Stock will continue to trade under the symbol “GM.” Item 5.03. Amendments to Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws; Change in Fiscal Year. On October 26, 2026, the Board approved amendments to the Company’s Amended and Restated Bylaws (as amended, the “Amended and Restated Bylaws”), which will become effective upon the commencement of trading of the Common Stock on Nasdaq. The Amended and Restated Bylaws were amended to update the applicable independence criteria under the definition of “Independent Director,” reflecting the Company’s expected listing on Nasdaq. The foregoing summary and description of the amendments to the Amended and Restated Bylaws does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Amended and Restated Bylaws, which is filed herewith as Exhibit 3.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K, and is incorporated herein by reference. Item 7.01. Regulation FD Disclosure. A copy of the press release issued by the Company announcing the transfer of its Common Stock listing to Nasdaq is attached as Exhibit 99.1 hereto and incorporated by reference into this Item 7.01. The information furnished pursuant to this Item 7.01, including Exhibit 99.1, shall not be considered “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), or otherwise subject to the liabilities of that section, and such information shall not be deemed incorporated by reference in any filing by the Company under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or the Exchange Act, except as may be expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing. title: General Motors Co 8-K exhibit 99.1 (press release)
text: EX-99.1 3 d53522dex991.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 News For Release: Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 6:30 a.m. ET GM Announces transfer of stock exchange listing to Nasdaq DETROIT, October 27, 2026 – General Motors (NYSE: GM) today announced that it will transfer the listing of its common stock, par value $0.01 per share (the “Common Stock”), to the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“Nasdaq”) from the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”). The Common Stock is expected to continue to be listed under the NYSE ticker symbol “GM” through market close on November 16, 2026. The company expects to begin trading as a Nasdaq-listed company on November 17, 2026. Following the transfer to Nasdaq, the Common Stock will continue to trade under the symbol “GM.” “GM’s customer-focused, technology-driven strategy is creating value for our stockholders, making Nasdaq a natural home for our listing as we grow,” said Paul Jacobson, GM Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. “We’re grateful for our long-standing partnership with the New York Stock Exchange and its remarkable legacy.” A Nasdaq listing provides eligibility for potential inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 Index ® . No action is required by existing stockholders with respect to the transfer of the company’s listing. General Motors (NYSE: GM) is driving the future of transportation, leveraging advanced technology to build safer, smarter, and lower emission cars, trucks, and SUVs. GM’s Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC brands offer a broad portfolio of innovative gasoline-powered vehicles and the industry’s widest range of EVs, as we move to an all-electric future. title: Message-board post about General Motors
text: Unconfirmed: a post on an investor message board claims the company plans to spin off its Cruise unit and sell a stake to a tech company within weeks, citing "people familiar with the matter." The post did not name its sources and General Motors did not respond to a request for comment. No filing or official statement supports the claim.

title: Air Plan Approval; California; Reasonable Further Progress Plan for the Coachella Valley Ozone Nonattainment Area
text: Air Plan Approval; California; Reasonable Further Progress Plan for the Coachella Valley Ozone Nonattainment Area (Environmental Protection Agency). The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or "the Agency") is proposing to approve a state implementation plan (SIP) revision from the State of California to meet the Clean Air Act (CAA) "Extreme" nonattainment area requirements for the Riverside County (Coachella Valley), California ozone nonattainment area ("Coachella Valley") for the 2008 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or "standards"). Specifically, the Agency is proposing to approve the reasonable further progress (RFP) demonstration and associated emissions inventory and motor vehicle emissions budgets ("budgets") for the Coachella Valley.

title: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review
text: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review (Environmental Protection Agency). The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing amendments to the New Source Performance Standards and Emission Guidelines for the Crude Oil and Natural Gas Source Category to address additional concerns raised with prior regulatory amendments finalized in March 2024. Specifically, the EPA is proposing changes in response to certain petitions for reconsideration of the March 2024 amendments, changes based on policy decisions and supporting legal interpretations, and changes that correct and clarify the regulatory text of the new source performance standards and emission guidelines. First, the EPA proposes to rescind the Super Emitter Program. Second, the EPA proposes to subcategorize different types of well sites affected and designated facilities to address issues related to the requirements finalized in March 2024 for marginal well sites and conventional well sites. Third, the EPA proposes changes to address issues related to liquids unloading, process controllers, pumps, fugitive emissions, storage vessels, covers and closed vent systems, equipment leaks at gas plants, and associated gas. Fourth, the EPA proposes changes to certain requirements finalized in March 2024 related to control devices and to provide owners and operators the option to conduct optical gas imaging surveys according to Appendix K for gas processing facilities. Lastly, the EPA proposes changes to correct inadvertent errors and to clarify regulatory language.
